skill.name: example-skill
skill.description: Demonstrates the structure, sections, workflow, and reference-file pattern for creating Claude Code skills.
skill.summary: Use a concise example to structure new AI skills.
skill.author: Joseph OBrien

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code and ordinary documentation text. I found no command execution, system reconnaissance behavior, prompt injection, network access, secret access, or data exfiltration intent.

static_findings.snippet: This skill includes reference files in `references/`:
- Document anti-patterns to avoid common mistakes

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 85 contains a Markdown inline-code path to a template file. It does not execute a shell command or instruct the model to run one.
Line 91 uses Markdown inline code to name the references directory. There is no Ruby backtick execution or command invocation.
Line 93 uses Markdown inline code for the file name structure-guide.md. The text is documentation and does not execute external commands.
Line 94 uses Markdown inline code for the file name examples.md. It is a documented reference and not executable shell syntax.
Line 66 tells authors to document anti-patterns. It does not gather system data, enumerate files, or inspect the host environment.

content.value_statement: Skill authors need a clear pattern for structure, workflow, and bundled references. This skill provides a concise example they can follow when creating Claude, Codex, or Claude Code skills.
actual_capabilities: Shows required YAML frontmatter fields for a skill.
Explains when to use an example skill as a reference.
Lists core principles for focused skill documentation.
Provides a four-step workflow for applying the example.
Identifies common anti-patterns for skill authors.
Links to a reference guide for structure details.
limitations: It is a documentation example, not an automation tool.
It does not create files or install dependencies.
It includes a reference to examples.md, but that file is not present.
It gives general guidance and not domain-specific skill content.

use_cases.title: Plan a First Skill
use_cases.description: Use the example to understand the expected sections before writing a new skill.

use_cases.title: Review Skill Structure
use_cases.description: Compare an existing skill against the example sections and documented anti-patterns.

use_cases.title: Improve Skill Documentation
use_cases.description: Check whether workflows, examples, and reference files are clear for future users.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the Skill Format
prompt_templates.prompt: Use example-skill to explain the required sections for a new skill. Keep the answer concise and include a checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Skill Outline
prompt_templates.scenario: Planning a new skill from the example.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use example-skill as a model. Draft an outline for a skill that helps with release notes.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Existing Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare my skill draft with example-skill. Identify missing sections, unclear workflow steps, and weak examples.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Publication Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Use example-skill and its structure guide to create a publication checklist for a team skill review process.

output_examples.input: Explain what sections my new skill should include.
output: When to Use: Define the trigger conditions.
What This Skill Does: State specific capabilities.
Workflow: Provide steps a user can follow.

output_examples.input: Review my skill draft for structure gaps.
output: The draft has a clear purpose and workflow.
Add an Anti-Patterns section to prevent common misuse.
Add a reference file only if it improves the user workflow.

output_examples.input: Help me prepare a team checklist for skill publication.
output_examples.output: The checklist should verify trigger conditions, frontmatter, workflow steps, examples, bundled references, and documented limitations.

best_practices: Use the example as a structural reference before writing domain content.
Keep each new skill focused on one clear capability.
Add reference files only when they improve the workflow.
anti_patterns: Do not copy placeholder content into a published skill.
Do not create broad skills that cover unrelated tasks.
Do not reference missing files in user-facing documentation.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It shows a simple structure for creating and reviewing AI skills.

faq.question: Does it create a new skill automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides documentation guidance that a user or agent can follow.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it include reference material?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a structure guide in the references directory.

faq.question: Is it safe to install?
faq.answer: The reviewed files contain documentation only. No executable behavior was found.

faq.question: What should authors watch for?
faq.answer: Authors should avoid broad scope, missing examples, and references to files that are not included.
